message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 18 November 2026 23:40 to 19 November 2026 23:40 UTC (20 November 05:10 IST). **Scope:** Products.txt only, plus the mandatory MongoDB ecosystem sweep. Listed products are not confirmation of installed versions or configurations.

Fresh reports warrant prompt review of NGINX, UniFi Access, and VMware Aria Operations / VMware Cloud Foundation deployments.

### NGINX: memory corruption vulnerabilities
**CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123634 and CVE-2026-113425.** Red Hat's 19 November bulletin assigns each a high CVSS 3.1 score of 8.1. Depending on configuration, remote unauthenticated traffic can crash workers or potentially execute code. The affected features include HTTP/2, HTTP/3, dynamic DNS resolution and mail proxying. NGINX is explicitly listed. These issues were originally disclosed on 18 November; the new Red Hat bulletin is within this scan window. [Red Hat bulletin](https://access.redhat.com/security/vulnerabilities/RHSB-2026-019).

**Additional NGINX issues: CVE-2026-118899, CVE-2026-120967, CVE-2026-123640 and CVE-2026-125283.** Debian's 19 November advisory newly reports these alongside the above issues; its combined advisory describes possible denial of service, information disclosure and certificate verification bypass, among other impacts. Individual severity and exact applicability to a deployment need checking. NGINX is listed, although the Debian package itself is not a separately listed product. [Debian advisory](https://lists.debian.org/debian-security-announce/2026/msg00564.html).

### Ubiquiti UniFi Access: seven vulnerabilities
**CVE-2026-132802 through CVE-2026-132808.** The 19 November CVE records cover UniFi Access Application flaws including unauthorized code execution, SQL injection, server-side request forgery, and certificate validation. Reported scores range from high 8.3 to critical 9.9. Ubiquiti/UniFi is listed; confirm whether UniFi Access is deployed and review affected versions. Ubiquiti's bulletin identifies the product and fixes. [Ubiquiti bulletin 073](https://community.ui.com/releases/Security-Advisory-Bulletin-073/677d5551-5ad9-4c85-86e9-4cdd9636a1e2); [19 November CVE records](https://installplango.com/research/cves/all/2026-11-19).

### VMware Aria Operations and Cloud Foundation: Apache HTTP/2
**CVE-2026-119618; VMSA-2026-0010.** A 19 November product-impact notice identifies VMware Aria Operations and VMware Cloud Foundation as affected by an Apache HTTP Server vulnerability. A reproduction of Broadcom's advisory reports critical severity, CVSS 9.8, and potential network-accessible code execution. Both VMware products are listed. The underlying Apache vulnerability was disclosed earlier; this is a newly reported VMware product impact, not a new Apache CVE. The Broadcom advisory could not be opened directly during this check, so confirm its current response matrix before acting. [Google Cloud product-impact notice](https://officially.news/p/01a1f59c-8df2-7077-867d-424abed5942a); [Broadcom advisory](https://support.broadcom.com/web/ecx/support-content-notification/-/external/content/SecurityAdvisories/0/39625).

### MongoDB ecosystem
No new MongoDB-family vulnerability was verified within the exact window. The dedicated sweep covered vendor alerts and searches across Server, mongod/mongos, Atlas services, Ops Manager and Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, database tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, and official libraries and integrations, including advisories without MongoDB in the title. Indexing and timestamp limitations mean this is not proof of absence. [MongoDB security alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts).

**Closing:** Prioritize review of exposed NGINX, UniFi Access and affected VMware deployments. Verify installed versions, configuration and vendor guidance. Search coverage is not exhaustive.
